submersion_dose.source: Federal Guidance Report No. 12 (EPA 402-R-93-081, 1993), Table III.1
submersion_dose.conclusion: Immersion dose rate alone (2.03 pSv/h) is ~320x higher than 6.3e-6 nSv/h, but still completely undetectable against 50-100 nSv/h background.

filter_accumulation.flow_rate_status: UNVERIFIED: EPA RadNet continuous sampler nominal flow rate ~35 CFM / ~60 m^3/h
filter_accumulation.conclusion: Filter accumulation could produce a measurable signal (16-30 CPM after 24h, 70-125 CPM after 100h) IF particulate iodine is retained and filter is not advanced.

honolulu_march21_alarms.interpretation: Honolulu triggered 2 alarms under Tier 4 on March 21 (07:00 and 08:00 UTC) with scores 0.9157 and 0.9530. Both occurred during dry weather (precip = 0 mm, 37-38 hours after rain). These alarms reflect subtle PMT baseline shifts in the maritime background rather than verified Fukushima plume detection, as Tier 3, Tier 2, and B4c remained unalarmed.
